newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 9.

text.p: Police have started an investigation into the collapse of Kiwi International Airlines. Detective Chief Inspector Rex Miller of Hamilton confirmed on Wednesday that aspects of the budget trans-Tasman airline's September liquidation were being investigated "as a result of documents forwarded to us by another government department". Founder Ewan Wilson said from Britain he had nothing to hide over the way the airline was run. The two-year-old company collapsed owing at least NZ$5 million, much of it in prepaid fares. Page 1.

A former Wellington pilot was killed when a Polynesian Airlines plane crashed on a hillside near the Western Samoan capital of Apia on Wednesday. Colin (Gus) Sydney Pyper, from Kelburn, was flying a twin-engined Otter aircraft when it ploughed into the hill. Two other people, a man from American Samoa and a woman from Western Samoa, were killed. Two people survived the crash, including a five-year-old girl whose father was among the dead. Page 1.

Waitangi Day commemoration organisers say Waitangi is the rightful place for celebrations but cannot guarantee protesters will not abuse guests. The official commemoration was moved to Wellington last year after protesters abused dignitaries and spat on the then governor-general Dame Catherine Tizard at Waitangi in 1995. Page 2.

Police Minister Jack Elder said on Wednesday he expected Parliament would be sympathetic to a proposal to cut the alcohol limit for drivers. Elder said cutting the alcohol limit was one suggestion put forward when he met senior police for his
briefing as police minister. It has been proposed that the limit be reduced from 80 milligrams of alcohol to 100 millilitres of blood, to 50 milligrams. Page 2.

Labour called on Wednesday for abolition of the School Certificate examination. "Its time has passed," said education spokesman Trevor Mallard. A spokeswoman for Education Minister Wyatt Creech said on Wednesday that a White Paper making recommendations about the future of the exam was expected to be made public within a few months. Page 2.

New Zealand companies involved in the Anzac frigate project stand to gain a share of a multi-billion-dollar programme to modernise the Philippines navy if an Australian company's tenders for parts of the project are successful. Transfield Defence Systems, the Melbourne-based company that is building the Anzac frigates, is preparing bids for two parts of the project -- three 80-metre patrol craft and two 56m fast-attack craft. If it succeeds, New Zealand companies that have been supplying Transfield with equipment for the Anzac frigates stand to gain more work on the Philippines contracts, Transfield spokesman Pat Wilson said from Melbourne on Wednesday. Page 13.
